source.title: Reconstructing Training Data with Informed Adversaries
source.authors: Borja Balle; Giovanni Cherubin; Jamie Hayes

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present, including appendices; no apparent cutoff or garbling that prevents extraction.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports its own measurements of training and test accuracy alongside reconstruction results, and says reconstruction success is not correlated with overfitting or standard membership inference success. These refine the catalog claim by showing that the tested reconstruction measure does not track the training–test gap in its CIFAR-10 settings.
record.gate_note: The paper studies reconstruction of training examples, not memorization of arbitrary labels or the claim versions' interventions and measures. Its training/test accuracies and explicit statement about overfitting bear on V7's measured-property question; reconstruction results are not rows for V8, which concerns removing selected examples and measuring test accuracy.
record.test_reason: The study measures training-data reconstruction, not any version's specified effect. Reconstruction error and accumulated gradient norms do not measure magnitude-aware sharpness or its association with generalization gaps (V7). Table X compares Adam with full-batch gradient descent with momentum, rather than the SGD comparison specified by V4.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. Standard MNIST and CIFAR-10 classifiers retain enough information for high-fidelity reconstruction by an informed adversary with unusually extensive knowledge. DP training mitigates the tested attacks with little utility loss in some regimes; the theoretical protection also depends on assumptions about the adversary's prior uncertainty.
record.recipe_differences: The paper trains classifiers and reconstructor networks to study individual training-data reconstruction, rather than fitting random labels and evaluating generalization. Its relevant analysis compares reconstruction error with gradient norms and reports training/test accuracy.
record.method_sensitivity: Reconstruction success varies with training epochs, activation, initialization knowledge, minibatch sampling seed, learning rate, and side-knowledge quantity. The authors report no apparent correlation between reconstruction success and overfitting across tested CIFAR-10 settings.

fits_no_version.finding: On MNIST, reconstruction MSE is weakly correlated with the target's accumulated gradient norm.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Accumulated target-gradient norm does not straightforwardly predict reconstruction fidelity in the tested informed-adversary setting.

fits_no_version.finding: Across the CIFAR-10 conditions in Table X, the authors report no apparent association between reconstruction success and overfitting or standard membership-inference success.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Successful informed-adversary reconstruction need not track the training–test accuracy gap or standard membership-inference vulnerability.

record.peer_reviewed: IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy (2022)
record.problems: The relevant comparison between reconstruction and overfitting is stated qualitatively; no correlation coefficient or uncertainty is provided. The paper's CIFAR-10 models have subpar test accuracy in the default setting and are trained with a reduced fixed set for shadow-data needs. Results are specific to the reconstruction attack and do not directly measure V7's training–test-gap property.
record.rows_left_out: No separate rows for other CIFAR-10 Table X conditions: the main table's numerous optimizer, fixed-set-size, and epoch combinations report separate train/test accuracies, but the authors' explicit overfitting-correlation statement is aggregate and the claim versions do not specify these model conditions. The table also includes membership AUC and reconstruction metrics, which do not measure the V7 gap or V8 removal effect. Figure 20's plotted values are not given numerically in the text; the stated weak-correlation result is retained in R1.

untested.parts: Coexistence of random-label fitting and natural-label generalization under the same architecture and recipe, including chance-level held-out performance with random labels.
Held-out error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error; width experiments measure reconstruction instead.
Convolutional versus fully connected held-out performance on the same image task and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD or momentum SGD under the specified tuning regimes and recovery interventions.
Batch-size effects on held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes; batch-size experiments report reconstruction metrics.
Dropout's effect on classifier held-out error across data sizes and regularization settings.
Magnitude-aware sharpness versus generalization gaps and comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures.
Test-accuracy effects of removing examples selected by label-memorization influence versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: Reporting training and test accuracy alone does not test V7. Likewise, reconstructing individual training images is distinct from fitting random labels in V1 and the example-removal intervention in V8.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out accuracy under natural labels.
Test error as width increases beyond interpolation.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and the tested norm- and margin-based comparisons; the paper measures reconstruction error against gradient norms, rather than the generalization-gap measure named in V7.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the resulting test-accuracy change.

rows.subject: MLP
rows.operation_detail: Compared reconstruction MSE per target with the sum of the target's gradient norms over training.
rows.measure: Relationship between reconstruction MSE and sum of gradient norms over training; described as weakly correlated.
rows.note: The paper says it is a weak correlation and explains that the expected inverse relation was not observed. This measures reconstruction ease, not the training–test gap or magnitude-aware sharpness.
rows.check: The weak correlation is correctly reported, but neither variable is the measure named in V7. An absent V7 effect cannot be inferred.
